question: A project lead is setting up a new recurring piece of work and is unsure which Claude model to use for it. What should she do first?
options: A) Pick the deepest-reasoning model, since starting with the strongest option is always safest.
B) Judge how much reasoning depth the work really needs, since that is what separates the tiers.
C) Pick the fastest and cheapest model, since a lighter model can be upgraded at any later point.
D) Ask Claude which of the available models it would recommend for the work she has described.
correct_answers: B) Judge how much reasoning depth the work really needs, since that is what separates the tiers.
explanations: Incorrect. The deepest tier consumes meaningfully more allowance, and reaching for it by default spends that budget on work that does not need it.
Correct. The tiers trade reasoning depth against speed and allowance, so the choice starts with an honest read of how hard the task actually is.
Incorrect. Defaulting to the lightest tier is the same mistake in the other direction, and it can hide a quality gap she never looks for.
Incorrect. That answer is generated from a general description rather than from her actual quality bar and constraints.
